The EU Single Market is based on a paradigm consumer who is a'sophisticated, well-informed, and alert' consumer who is able to take care of himself or herself and who is able to make his own decisions.
the concept of the paradigm consumer is a useful tool in EU Single Market law, but it does not suffice to protect consumers.
the EU consumer is the cornerstone of EU single market law and that the EU has a long way to go to make sure that consumers can enjoy the benefits of the Single Market and the EU consumer policy.

the following questions: (1) How can the EU Single Market be made to work for consumers?
the role of the consumer in the European Union.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paradigm of a 'paradigmatic consumer' has become more important than ever before, but the concept itself has not yet reached the status of a 'European consumer'.
EU Single Market law is not a threat to consumers.
the EU has not yet found the paradigm consumer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Single Market is a success story.
the EU consumer policy has been developed in a way that is in line with the EU Single Market.
the Single Market is a consumer market and the consumer is the Single Market.
The main takeaway from our work is that

EU consumer policy should be based on a strong paradigm of consumer and that this concept of consumer should not be limited to a single type of consumer but should be broadened to cover the different types of consumers that exist in the EU.
the EU consumer is not a 'paradigmal' consumer, but a consumer who has the right to be protected and informed and is able to make informed decisions.
EU consumer policy is not a static concept but is constantly evolving and adapting to the needs of the European consumer and society.
